articleTitle: A global comparison of ramp-metering algorithms optimising traffic distribution on motorways and arterials
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The objective of this paper is to compare different ramp-metering algorithms in terms of the compromise they establish between delays to traffic on motorways and on arterial roads. Two different types of local ramp-metering were compared: ALINEA algorithm with a feedback philosophy and Demand-Capacity algorithm with a feed-forward philosophy. The main conclusion of this work is that an integrated policy is necessary between motorway and arterial road operators while implementing traffic control policies such as ramp-metering. The choice of a combination of ramp-metering algorithm, green time policy and ramp queue management strategy should consider impacts on the entire road system. This work has also shown that this choice may be different depending on the traffic condition on the motorway and the arterials. Further research can be devoted to developing an algorithm that will identify the best ramp-metering algorithm during a given traffic situation.

articleTitle: Detection of night-time road lines captured from a moving platform for the purpose of retro-reflective quality assessment
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: A robust method for the extraction of road lines from an image is proposed. The images, captured from a moving platform, are of a night-time road scene. All images are tagged with synchronised global positioning (GPS) data. The images, once captured, are then stored and processed offline. The road lines are detected using a support vector machine (SVM). It is proposed that a photometric analysis is then carried out on the extracted line data and a database of effective and defective road lines and their locations is compiled.

articleTitle: Modelling adaptive control - a reality?
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Traffic microsimulation tools are now widely accessible and modelling in support of planning applications and as evidence in Transport Assessments is becoming common place. This paper questions the requirement to accurately model signal operation in microsimulation models and explores whether modelling using an adaptive control methodology results in a more accurate and ‘implementation friendly’ model. The article looks at available studies around the issues of signal control and its associated network behaviour as well as making some comparisons between real world data and a simulated intersection.

articleTitle: Sensor integration for mobile mapping and feature analysis
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The ITS (Intelligent Transportation Systems) group at the Institute of Technology Blanchardstown (ITB) has been working on issues in the automated analysis of road signage and delineation since 2002. This research is concerned with the detection and analysis of road signage and raised pavement markers from image data. This involved the design and construction of a prototype portable mobile mapping system that linked GPS to machine vision data. A new mobile mapping system has now been developed that is distinguished from its predecessors by its ability to give survey-grade geo-referenced positions for substandard delineation [7]. The new system also logs and presents in real-time the data supplied by all the different sensor systems together under a common graphical user interface.

articleTitle: How does the use of a continuously updating database allow for the analysis of a user's changing behaviour in electric vehicles?
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Environmental considerations and a physical lack of fossil fuels mean that continuing to fuel cars by internal combustion, in the long term, is unviable. To combat this it is necessary to look at other methods of powering vehicles. One such option is the electric powered car and this is reflected in the large amount of support and R&D monies that government and other bodies are investing in this technology and the underlying support infrastructure of charging points and supply.

articleTitle: Development of algorithms to improve ramp metering system in England
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Ramp metering (RM) has been deployed in more than 80 locations on the Highways Agency (HA) motorway network. Evaluation of operational sites shows average journey time reductions of 13% [3]. Experience gained during the installation, calibration and operation of the first 30 sites suggested that further benefits could be generated from the ramp metering system by further development of certain aspects of the system algorithms. This paper details the four key proposed algorithm developments and the expected performance improvements as suggested by detailed modelling work [1].

articleTitle: M25 Speed Harmonisation
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The M25 Speed Harmonisation project was a highly effective congestion management tool, installed on the anti-clockwise section of the M25 between Junction 28 and Junction 27. An innovative approach was taken, combining pVMS, SPECS type ANPR cameras, a central Journey Time Management Server (JTMS) and wireless General Packet Radio Service (GPRS) communications. The JTMS would anticipate flow breakdown by monitoring average vehicle speeds and traffic volumes. If such conditions occurred advisory 50 miles per hour (mph) limit would be displayed on five roadside pVMS. During its operational period it reduced congestion and minimised flow breakdown. In conjunction with the positive effects on congestion no injury collisions were reported during the operational period.

articleTitle: Modelling of algorithms to improve RM system in England
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The Highways Agency has installed ramp metering at over 80 sites in England, with evaluation results showing an average 13% reduction in journey times [1]. Despite the success of the existing system, some potential improvements have been identified. Due to the complexity of the algorithms, the improvements were modelled using the micro-simulation package VISSIM [2]. This paper describes the method and results of the modelling. The modelling exercise has shown that all the algorithms have worked as expected. It has also shown that all the algorithms designed could provide additional performance benefits over the existing system.

articleTitle: Standards-based RTI. A new approach
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Over the last few years standards have been developing related to integrating real-time bus information. The RTIG specifications have been successful in enabling server to server connections between systems. These connections enable adjacent control systems to exchange data about cross-border services.

articleTitle: New developments for bus priority at traffic signals in London using iBus
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Buses in London play a vital role in the movement of the people in the capital. Recognising their importance, Transport for London (TfL) is continuing to implement a variety of measures to help buses. Among these measures, a recent addition is the implementation of a new automatic vehicle location (AVL) system for the bus fleet - iBus. TfL is now looking into various ways of giving bus priority at traffic signals using this facility. This paper will initially summarise the status of bus priority at traffic signals in London at the point iBus was introduced (2007–09). The paper will continue with a summary of the Research and Development process which has been proceeding alongside iBus commissioning, and results to date. R&D has been ongoing so that best use can be made of the new facilities in iBus for bus priority, once its ‘basic’ operational functioning has been confirmed. In broad terms, the new opportunities concern enhanced bus detection and new priority strategies.

articleTitle: Simulation study on improving traffic safety and traffic flow in the vicinity of a motorway accident through vehicle-to-vehicle communication
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Vehicle breakdowns and crashes on motorways can create a sudden drop in traffic speed and make driving conditions dangerous through the requirement of many merging manoeuvres within a confined region. Ideal response strategies are not possible throughout all of the motorway network (lane closure and speed reduction by overhead signs), and temporary instructional equipment takes time to arrive. Modern vehicle communications technologies will soon allow drivers to be alerted much sooner to an accident, and voluntarily take action to ensure smoother and safer traffic flow. Here, we test a driver advice system for unexpected lane closure, using a radio communication simulator built into a microscopic traffic simulation package. It is shown that even a small number of equipped and cooperative drivers could help prevent dangerous oscillations of traffic flow around the merge point and increase the level of safety while the obstruction is cleared. The system has been developed within the EU project SOCIONICAL, where simulations are developed to examine socio-technical systems that may aid people during situations of emergency.

articleTitle: Benefits of automatic crash notification for traffic management
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: eCall is an eSafety technology giving automatic notification of vehicles involved in “a crash situation” to the emergency services, whilst the vehicle is in a mobile phone coverage area. The principal benefits of eCall are reported to be safety-related; alerting emergency services to the exact location of an incident allows quicker and more effective medical assistance. However, recent work for the Highways Agency [1] and for the European Commission [6] have, for the first time, identified and quantified the potential benefits in utilising eCall data for traffic management and congestion reduction. This paper briefly reviews the European situation with eCall and describes some of the potential implications for the HA if eCall were implemented in the UK.

articleTitle: Comparison of signalized junction control strategies that use localization probe data
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: This paper presents a simulation test bed and a methodology for evaluating urban signalized junction control algorithms that use localization probe data from all vehicles in the local area. The simulator is based on SIAS Paramics microsimulation software with bespoke software modules built on top for automatic network generation, localization data processing and signal control. Also presented are results from tests carried out using the simulation test bed to evaluate localization strategies. The tested strategies use a hierarchical structure of auctioning agents. Results from tests on an isolated signalized junction indicate that the performance of the auctioning agent algorithms compare favourably with the MOVA algorithm using inductive loop data. Results are also presented for tests on a twin junction where strategies are synchronized. These show a significant improvement in performance through synchronization.

articleTitle: Accelerated delivery of Managed Motorways: Birmingham box phase 1
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The Birmingham Box Managed Motorways Phases 1 & 2 (BB MM 1&2) project is deploying Managed Motorways (MM) technology and operational regimes onto the M40, M42 and M6 in England. Phase 1 was completed in November 2009 and Phase 2 is currently being constructed. The Project Team achieved successful delivery of Phase 1 within the constraints of an accelerated programme, going from the commencement of detailed design, tender through construction and into operation in approximately two years. This paper examines some of the techniques used to plan, manage and deliver the rapid deployment of a complex, operationally led technology scheme, focussing on Phase 1 of the project.

articleTitle: Technology contributions towards a sustainable transport system
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Transport Technology systems, applications and services are increasingly recognised as playing a high profile and vital role in the achievement of transportation objectives and carbon reduction targets. This paper presents a case that transport technology systems and services are key enablers, leading to the development of smarter infrastructure.

articleTitle: Ongoing development of an adaptive CCTV Display system for incident detection for the Highways Agency
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Adaptive CCTV Display aims to allow operators to detect incidents more effectively using existing CCTV cameras. Alerts from CCTV automatic incident detection (AID) systems are combined with live data from inductive loops and historic data to identify sections of the road network where incidents may have occurred. Images of these discrete sections of road are then displayed to operators. Using AID on existing pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) cameras typically gives an unacceptably high false-alarm rate. This is mitigated by probabilistic data-fusion and an effective but unobtrusive display. A prototype system has allowed operators to detect incidents around 3 minutes faster than without the system. Work to enhance the system will increase its long-term maintainability, improve its user interface, and enhance the data fusion algorithms at its core. These data fusion enhancements will see the system make use of richer information from underlying AID systems and present to users with more information on the likely cause of an alert.

articleTitle: M42 Active Traffic Management monitoring and evaluation: Results from Hard Shoulder Running up to 60 mph
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Active Traffic Management (ATM) schemes (now called Managed Motorways) aim to address congestion and improve Journey Time Reliability (JTR) by utilising a set of advanced Intelligent Transport Systems applications to make as much use of the available capacity as possible. This paper presents the results obtained from the impact assessment of Hard Should Running up to 60 mph on traffic conditions over the M42-ATM section. The analysis does not cover safety data as at least 3 years worth of safety data is required for a valid safety analysis.

articleTitle: A bilevel time-dependent scheduling model for hazmat road transportation
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The currently most hazmat transportation scheduling models mainly aim to minimize total costs in order to take into both transportation out-of-pocket expenses and risk-related costs which are viewed as static. In this work, we consider the following hazmat transportation routing strategies problem: a given set of hazmat shipments has to be shipped over a road transportation network in order to transport a given amount of hazardous materials from a specific origin point to a specific destination within the time limitation. Here we mainly concern how time factors affect hazmat transportation routing selection through accident rates and the number of suffered people(in-road, off-road and cener), and provide a bilevel time-dependent programming formulation represents the distinct decisions made by the government and the carrier for hazmat transportation scheduling problem. Then we separated the problems into two parts for solving the model. At first, we solve the outer and inner problems of the bilevel model iteratively on modified/restricted graphs. Secondly we provide a heuristic for the time-dependent shortest model. The proposed bilevel model and heuristic algorithm are experimented on real scenarios of a regional network.

articleTitle: Exploration of traffic performance measures for exclusive Motorcycle lane at diverging and basic segment facilities
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Private vehicles are still the most commonly used mode of transport in Malaysia and the usage is becoming more significant nowadays for both long and short distance travel. Statistic shows that the number of vehicles on Malaysian roads is increasing annually. Thus, with the increase in the number of vehicles in the near future, the need to provide good road infrastructure is becoming more significant. As a developing country, the era of road infrastructure design and construction is expected to be on going in the near future to cater for an increasing traffic demand. An exclusive Motorcycle lane, EML is constructed with the objective of providing mobility and safety to motorcyclist where users are travelling with high level of safety. Based on current practice, EML is designed based on the objective that segregation traffic is better than mixed traffic for motorcyclist safety.

articleTitle: The CEDAR project: Time, distance, place (TDP) road pricing
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: CEDAR (Charging Electronically by Distance And Road) was a technology and behavioural trial of distance-based road user charging in urban areas of Southern England, using GPS-based On-Board Equipment (OBE) to improve transport logistics and reduce congestion, extending the successful trials Thales previously carried out for Transport for London. The CEDAR project ran from May 2008 to December 2009, with the trial running during the latter 6 months of 2009, and was a successful demonstration of the technology. We conclude that the technology is close to being acceptable for commercial use in real urban road pricing schemes

articleTitle: Reductions in fuel consumption and CO2 emissions with specs average speed enforcement
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Data was gathered on passenger car fuel consumption at various speeds, and compared with traffic speed profiles for unenforced motorways and motorways enforced with SPECS average speed cameras to determine the potential fuel savings and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> reductions that may be achieved by enforcing the national speed limit on UK motorways.

articleTitle: ITS (UK) strategy to support carbon reduction and to address climate change issues
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Climate change and carbon reduction represent a significant challenge for the UK as a whole. The ambitious targets for carbon reduction in the short term (up to 2022) present a significant challenge to the transport sector. For ITS technology and the ITS industry there is a significant opportunity to assist and support the transport sector in reducing carbon emissions. This paper should be seen as a step in the journey to reducing carbon emissions from the transport sector. The next step is to engage the industry in a dialogue around the opportunities outlined in this document. There is a workshop organised by the ITS (UK) Carbon Working Group on 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> July 2010 at Newcastle University to help facilitate the process of engagement . The views of the ITS (UK) Interest Groups and other interested parties will be sought in the run up to the workshop. After the workshop it is anticipated that this strategy will be expanded and updated.

articleTitle: Fusion of journey time data using error distributions
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Data fusion is a general term used to describe techniques for combining multiple sources of information, often from highly disparate sources, to produce a single ‘best estimate’ or ‘best decision’. Whilst there are a wide variety of methods in use, the scientific logic that underpins them (or is used to justify them) can generally be expressed in terms of relatively simple probability theory. The idea of constructing a data fusion method for inter-urban traffic data that is based solely on the logic of probability theory is explored and found to have potential. An example of fusion between journey time data from GPS-equipped vehicles and Automated Number Plate Recognition cameras shows that the fused journey time is considerably closer to the benchmark (from MIDAS inductive loops) than that from either of the individual sources. Although the fundamental principles are established, this method is not fully developed here. There are a number of unresolved issues surrounding how one should optimally parameterise the system and how, in the absence of ubiquitous data, one can reliably determine the requisite distribution functions which describe the relationships between variables.

articleTitle: Towards a pro-active model for identifying motorway traffic risks using individual vehicle data from double loop detectors
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: This paper presents a methodology to develop motorway traffic risk identification models using individual vehicle traffic data, meteorological data and crash database for a study site at a two-lane-per-direction section on motorway A1 in Switzerland. We define traffic situations (TSs) representing traffic status for three-minute interval and traffic regimes obtained by clustering TSs. The models are traffic regimes - based and are developed using Regression Trees to identify rear-end collision risks. Interpreting results shows that speed variance on the right lane and speed difference between two lanes are the two main causes of rear-end crashes. We also compare the results obtained from three-minute TSs with the results obtained from five-minute TSs using the same methodology.

articleTitle: Network ATM Supervisory Subsystem (NASS): Improving the use of Managed Motorways
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The Network ATM Supervisory Subsystem (NASS) is a unique software tool which has been developed to pro-actively assist in the management and control of the motorway network.

articleTitle: Autonomous VMS Switching from Positional Information Of Gritters
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The Autonomous VMS Switching from Positional Information of Gritters (AVSPIG) project demonstrates the feasibility of automating the process of Control Centre operators manually switching Variable Message Signs (VMS) to show ‘Gritting in Progress’ when winter treatments are underway. Using an on-board Global Positioning System (GPS) unit to provide regular updates on the position of the Winter Service Vehicle (WSV), the signs within a predetermined distance are identified and, without any operator intervention, a suitable message is displayed. Similarly, once a WSV is no longer in the vicinity of a particular sign, the message is removed to ensure that only accurate and relevant information is communicated to the public. Trials in 2009 successfully demonstrated this proof of concept system.

articleTitle: Development of a hard shoulder monitoring system (HASMOS)
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: HASMOS is a system that has been developed in partnership by the Highways Agency (HA), WSP and its supply chain. Its ultimate objective is to enable Regional Control Centre (RCC) operators to monitor the motorway hard shoulder for obstructions by exception. HASMOS began as a project to research the feasibility of fusing disparate vehicle detector data and has progressed to its current status as a proof of concept using scanning millimetre wave radar as the primary means of detection. The most recent work has involved an on-road evaluation of HASMOS on the M42, which has shown the technology to be effective and has highlighted some areas for further development.

articleTitle: A model for safe and secure execution of downloaded vehicle applications
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Existing secure protocols and code signing mechanisms for vehicle systems to download and install software over the air certify only the origin and the integrity of software; thus, they do not address errors that might not be detected in the development process and cannot ensure that the downloaded software do not contain malicious code. In this paper, we identify such possible threats by developing a threat model for the vehicle software architecture. We propose countermeasures against the threats by preventing or modifying inappropriate behaviour caused by, e.g., malicious or poorly designed applications. We propose a model to deploy the approach which is based on modifying the application at the wireless gateway in the vehicle before being installed. As a result, security policies are embedded into the application and intercepts security relevant execution events. Thus, the execution of downloaded vehicle applications is monitored to ensure the safety and security for the vehicle system and to detect potential cyber attacks.

articleTitle: R-TIS: Real time travel information system for multi-modal real time information for Southampton Airport, the Olympic Park and the London Transport Museum
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: This paper focuses on the provision of real time travel information to transport network users and will discuss the processes in establishing agreements with transport providers to gain reliable access to their real time data for use on real time travel information displays (R-TIS). The paper will then move on to discuss the software and hardware architecture used to implement the system and why we chose this route. We will discuss the differing presentation styles of displaying the real time information depending on its environment and the behaviour of the people interacting with the displays. Finally, the paper will report on the feedback we have received from the users of the systems and how wider adoption of the technology could lead to increased public transport uptake.

articleTitle: Ramp metering - integrating strategic and local road networks
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Ramp metering is a traffic management tool widely used by the Highways Agency (HA) to help keep motorway traffic moving at busy junctions. Through partnership with Local Highways Authorities (LHA) with the use of Integrated Traffic Management and Integrated Network Management it is hoped that ramp metering can be a key tool in the better management of the strategic and inter urban road network.

articleTitle: On the rebound: How can we meet our carbon targets in light of rebound effects?
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Purpose of this paper is to estimate the rebound effects of innovative traffic management and public transport systems. This paper reviews what rebound effects are and how they apply to transport for technologies such as fuel efficient vehicles, telecommuting, e-commerce and fuel prices. We will identify innovations and best practice for sustainable transport strategies around the world, and make a wide ranging set of recommendations on how we can meet our carbon targets without falling short because of rebound effects.

articleTitle: Well Maintained Electronic Traffic Systems
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The Code of Practice for Well Maintained Electronic Traffic Systems has been written by Atkins on behalf of the UK Roads Liaison Group. The project has been managed by the Department for Transport and has been supported by a Steering Group of knowledgeable maintenance managers from a number of local authorities around the United Kingdom. This paper deals with a number of issues, including: • Current position (background) • Development of the Code • Purpose of the Code • Objectives • Relationship with other guidance • Intended readership • Scope of the Code • Management of all highway assets • Status of the Code • Conclusions • Acknowledgements

articleTitle: Get the picture: How digital camera images are changing the way we travel
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The Highways Agency in England has business objectives to deliver safer roads, reliable journeys and informed travellers. The Highways Agency has installed over 1,500 CCTV cameras on the strategic road network to support its operational requirements (see Figure 1).

articleTitle: Enhanced interoperability and communications for the Highways Agency and English motorways
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: This paper describes a project initiative aimed at providing a self-establishing, self-healing IP-based broadband network, and associated applications, for enhancing communications at major incidents and disasters. This project forms part of a programme of continued improvement for the Highways Agency's Traffic Officer Service, and aims to provide a framework which will lead to full inter-working and data sharing with the emergency services.

articleTitle: Economics of traffic signals
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The decision as to whether to install traffic signals or not is often based on a need to manage traffic and pedestrian conflicts at peak periods. Rarely is account taken of the economic impacts of traffic signals and how these may change as a result of varying traffic compositions, journey purposes and time of day. Using actual traffic data from selected junctions in London this paper addresses this failing and concludes that in the right place and at the right time traffic signals can provide significant economic benefits but in certain circumstances there are greater benefits from switching traffic signals off.

articleTitle: Results of an innovative Dutch traffic management programme - FileProof
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: In 2006 The Dutch Ministry of Transport, Public Works and Water Management started a programme which was called FileProof. The aim of the programme was to find, analyse and implement relatively simple solutions for the short term alleviation of congestion. The programme comprised three project streams: 1. Projects to limit regular congestion 2. Projects to limit congestion due to incidents 3. Projects to induce alternative choices by drivers to reduce congestion In total almost 60 projects were executed. In general, the cost of the projects was low and their effect significant, rendering them very good value for money. This together with the fast implementation makes FileProof a successful programme.

articleTitle: Addressing the impact of road scheme complexity on the driver: Development of a software tool to analyse driver workload arising from its road features and other infrastructure
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: As road scheme design including ITS features, has a direct impact on the behaviour of drivers and consequently on road safety, understanding the demands placed on the driver by different scheme designs is critical. This paper outlines the purpose for investigating driver workload and scheme design, the applicable science and the development of a software tool created to allow scheme designers to predict driver workload. The tool can be used to isolate infrastructure arrangements such as message signs and signals and other design features contributing to high workload. The designer can trial alternative scheme designs to evenly spread driver workload and consequently the potential for human error.

articleTitle: Operational challenges of Managed Motorways
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: Managed Motorways are being deployed as an alternative to road widening. They allow the capacity of the motorway to be dynamically controlled both automatically and by direct intervention from control room based operational staff in response to fluctuating traffic demand. To operate Managed Motorways safely and effectively, there is a greater reliance on technology than conventional roads, coupled with an increased requirement for operational contribution. Focusing investment on the enhanced use of technology delivers tangible benefits to the travelling public, and appropriate use and operation of technology can lead to compliant driver behaviour that brings significant benefits to the network. However, in order for these benefits to be realised, the technology required must be maintained to a sufficient standard to allow the network to be safely operated in accordance with the correct procedures. While the concept of ‘Design for Maintenance’ is widely used and understood, the concept of ‘Design for Operation’ is a more novel concept that is explored further in this paper.

articleTitle: Automatic road feature detection and correlation for the correction of consumer satellite navigation system mapping
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for the use of on-vehicle video analysis aimed at the verification and correction of consumer satellite navigation system mapping information. The proposed system automatically detects road and environment features (e.g. flyover bridges, road junctions, traffic lights and road signs) for real-time comparison to information available from corresponding navigation mapping. This can be used both for secondary feature-based localization of vehicle position and the verification of roadway mapping information against the true environment.

articleTitle: Exploration of 85th percentile operating speed model on horizontal and vertical alignments: A case study for two lane rural highways
publicationTitle: IET Road Transport Information and Control Conference and the ITS United Kingdom Members' Conference (RTIC 2010) - Better transport through technology
abstract: The increase number of accidents on two lane rural highways have been linked or related with the problem of inconsistencies on the operating speed and geometric design of highways. Facts showed that traffic collisions have become a major source of social and econometric losses in recent years in Malaysia. The country facing a serious road accident problem and every year for the last five years which more than 5000 people was killed on road. Despite of that, more intention to road safety has to be made so that the traffic collisions due to sub-standard and inconsistency of highway design can be reduced and eliminated. For highway and street design consistency, the quantitative method that has been used mainly by United States is the design speed concept. Whereas, research and experience from other countries such as Germany, Australia and Switzerland indicates that operating speed concept in the design consistency analysis of two lane rural highways is more effective in detecting inconsistencies. This research paper presents an empirical research and presents the new equation to estimate the 85<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> percentile operating speed model for the horizontal and vertical curve tangent that reflective on Malaysian rural highways conditions. A speed measurement was taken at twelve sites and regression equations were developed to predict the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">85</inf> of vehicles on horizontal and vertical of alignments on two lane rural highways. The developed V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">85</inf> model presented intends to detect geometric design inconsistencies in most of the horizontal and vertical alignment. And lastly, this research is an attempt to harmonize the designer adoption in selecting and designing highway and the road users' expectation while on the wheels towards an ergonomic approach.
